title: Geometric component count is locally constant in a proper smooth family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $s\in S$, let $n(s)$ be the number of connected components of $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$, where $\overline{\kappa(s)}$ is an algebraic closure of the residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $n(s)$ is finite and $n:S\to\mathbf N$ is locally constant, including $n(s)=0$ for empty fibres. In particular, if $X_s$ is geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], there is an open neighbourhood of $s$ on which every fibre is geometrically connected.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, specialized to smooth morphisms (smooth implies flat with geometrically reduced fibres)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], the assumed smooth $f$ is flat. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], its geometric fibres are reduced. The properness and finite-presentation hypotheses are already assumed. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), both $X_s$ over $\kappa(s)$ and $X_{\bar s}$ over $\overline{\kappa(s)}$ are proper. The description in [def-weil-geometric-fibre] identifies the latter with the field-extension base change of $X_s$.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, hypotheses; smooth specialization uses Tags 01VF and 056T

proof.text: Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $q=0$. The module $\mathcal O_X$ is free of rank one over itself, hence of finite presentation, and is flat over $S$: at $x$ its stalk is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, flat over $\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}$ by [def-weil-flat-morphism] and Step 1. Its pullback to a fibre is that fibre's structure sheaf. Thus $A_s=H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is finite-dimensional and $\beta(s)=\dim_{\kappa(s)}A_s$ is upper semicontinuous. No reducedness of $S$ is needed: the reduced-base hypothesis belongs only to clause (3), which is not used.

source.place: Tag 0BDN, label lemma-jump-loci-geometric, finiteness of fibre cohomology and upper semicontinuity (source clause (2)), applied to the structure sheaf

proof.text: Fix $s$, put $k=\kappa(s)$ and $K=\overline{k}$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover]. Apply the affine-base clause of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Properness includes finite type and thus quasi-compactness by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Its diagonal is a closed immersion; the inverse image of any affine open under the diagonal is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence quasi-compact, giving quasi-separatedness by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Its structure sheaf is quasi-coherent: on an affine chart it is the sheaf associated to the ring itself. This gives $A_s\otimes_k K\cong\Gamma(X_{\bar s},\mathcal O_{X_{\bar s}})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product], the right side is $\prod_{c\in C_s}K$ with $C_s$ finite, because Step 1 gives properness and reducedness. Tensoring a finite $k$-basis of $A_s$ gives a $K$-basis of $A_s\otimes_kK$ (identify $A_s$ with $k^d$ using that basis and tensor the inverse coordinate maps); the coordinate vectors of $K^{C_s}$ form a basis indexed by $C_s$. Therefore $\beta(s)=|C_s|=n(s)$. For an empty fibre both vector spaces are zero and both dimensions are zero.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, identification of component count with zeroth cohomology dimension; Tag 0BUG and flat base change

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-proper-component-count-lower-semicontinuous] to $f$, using flatness from Step 1 and the assumed properness and finite presentation. It gives for every $s$ an open neighbourhood $V_s$ on which $n(t)\geq n(s)$. This uses no geometric reducedness, and proves the lower-semicontinuity half of the argument.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, first sentence, invoking Tag 0BUI

proof.text: For every $s$, upper semicontinuity of $\beta=n$ from Steps 2 and 3 gives an open neighbourhood $W_s$ on which $n(t)<n(s)+1$, hence $n(t)\leq n(s)$ since these values are integers. On $V_s\cap W_s$ this and Step 4 force $n(t)=n(s)$. This proves local constancy, also at $n(s)=0$. Finiteness was established in Step 3. If $S$ is empty the pointwise assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, final sentence: lower and upper semicontinuity imply local constancy

proof.text: If $X_s$ is geometrically connected, [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] makes $X_{\bar s}$ connected and nonempty, so $n(s)=1$. Take the neighbourhood from Step 5. For every $t$ there, $n(t)=1$, so $X_{\bar t}$ is connected: its sole connected component is the whole nonempty space. The reverse implication of [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure], over $\kappa(t)$, shows that $X_t$ is geometrically connected. Thus this is exactly the claimed open neighbourhood, and an empty fibre is never erroneously treated as connected.

source.place: Tags 0387 (lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected) and 054N (lemma-geometrically-connected-check-after-extension), algebraically closed extension criterion; consequence of Tag 0E0N
